title: itembank treatment recommendation contract
description: The contract a provider candidate is validated against before any field of it is read. Provider output is untrusted input: director.validate_recommendation calls schema_validate.validate first and reads nothing until it returns clean, so a malformed candidate cannot reach a field access. A candidate failing this schema is refused with director.recommendation_invalid and is never partially applied; there is no path that accepts the fields that happened to validate. A candidate whose treatment_kind is outside the closed eleven-member vocabulary is refused with director.unknown_treatment_kind. Validating is not accepting: a candidate that passes this schema is a proposal, and it becomes durable course state only when a rights check against the live registry permits the bind.

objective_id.description: The objective this recommendation is for. One objective per recommendation.

treatment_kind.description: One of the eleven treatment kinds in TREAT-01, or the empty string. The empty string is how a provider says it has no recommendation for this objective; it is not a twelfth treatment kind, and no code path treats it as one. direct-reading is a complete result: an objective the source already teaches well needs no generated artifact, and recommending direct-reading is a finished recommendation rather than a refusal to recommend.

rationale.description: Why this treatment, in the provider's own words. Always read as synthesis, never as a source passage; see synthesis below.

synthesis.description: Always true, by construction. A rationale is always model synthesis and is never a source passage, and a const is what makes that label structural rather than a convention a reader has to remember. A provider cannot mark a rationale as quoted source text, because there is no value of this field that says so.

confidence.description: The provider's stated confidence in the treatment choice. Advisory only: it never gates a bind, and unknown is not an error.

coverage.description: The objective-to-source coverage claim this recommendation rests on. Every claim carries a stable locator and a match_kind, so a reader can tell a located claim from a guessed one.

state.description: One of the five coverage states. unknown is restrictive and is never a lesser form of covered.

locator.description: Where in the source the claim points. A coverage claim points at a locator and reproduces nothing.

confidence.description: The provider's stated confidence in the coverage claim, separate from its confidence in the treatment choice.

source_object_id.description: The source object the locator resolves inside.

match_kind.description: How the claim was matched. heading-similarity is a weaker proof than locator and must never on its own produce a covered state; that rule is enforced in director.py, and this field is what makes the enforcement possible.

alternatives.description: Treatments the provider considered and did not choose. Recorded so a reviewer sees what was passed over rather than only what was picked.

treatment_kind.description: The alternative treatment, from the same closed vocabulary.

confidence.description: The provider's stated confidence in the alternative.

citations.description: The source spans this recommendation was built from. A recommendation with no citations is a recommendation with nothing behind it, and the key is required so its absence is a refusal rather than an empty default.
